title: Lark and the Wobbly Pebble
markdown:
Bright sunshine burst through the window, tickling Lark’s nose. Dawn cracked! Birds twittered a cheerful, chirpy song. Today was definitely going to be an ADVENTURE kind of day! She practically bounced out of bed, her bright red rubber boots practically jumping to be worn. Outside, Nibbles the otter was already darting through the dewdrops, his sleek, dark fur sparkling like a thousand tiny diamonds. The cool morning air tickled her cheeks as she stepped onto the damp grass.

"Lark! Lark! Come quick!" Nibbles chittered, wiggling his whiskers with pure excitement. His little, beady eyes practically popped. He pointed a tiny, wet paw towards a tall glass jar sitting on Ms. Rowan’s sun-dappled porch. Inside, a perfectly straight, familiar striped pebble looked all bendy, like a candy cane that had been left too close to a hot fire and gone completely wobbly.

"Goodness gracious me," tutted Ms. Rowan, peering at it with her spectacles perched on her nose. Her kind smile was a little puzzled. "That pebble was as straight as a ruler when I put it in this morning. Now it looks like a particularly twisted pretzel! Most peculiar."

Lark blinked, her quick mind already whirring. She poked the pebble gently through the glass. It stayed stubbornly wobbly. She carefully scooped some of the cool, clear water out with a tiny fishing net. The pebble looked straight again! But the moment she carefully placed it back into the jar with the water… bendy it was again! "This is truly peculiar," Lark declared, her brow furrowed in deep thought. "It’s the water! It must be the water doing something!"

Nibbles bobbed his head enthusiastically, his sleek tail giving a happy slap on the porch. "Yes, yes! The water does it! The water is tricky!" He grabbed a long, dry twig from the edge of the garden and dipped it into the jar. It looked like it had snapped right in half! "Look! The twig’s broken!" he squeaked, pointing again.

Lark giggled, a bright, tinkling sound. "It’s not broken, Nibbles. It just looks that way. It’s a trick!" She bravely dipped her own finger into the cool water. Her finger, all nice and straight and familiar, seemed to curve quite noticeably at the water’s edge. "See? My finger looks bent too! It's like magic!"

Ms. Rowan clasped her hands together, a little gasp escaping her. "Well, I never! How can plain old water do such a thing?"

Suddenly, Lark had an idea. A brilliant, sparkly idea! She dashed to the shed and grabbed a small, shiny flashlight. Back on the porch, she carefully darkened the area by pulling a curtain. "Now watch this!" she whispered. She switched on the flashlight, pointing its beam towards the water in the jar. At first, the light beam shot straight. But then—whoosh!—as it hit the water’s surface and plunged in, the beam seemed to bend downwards. It didn’t go straight through!

"Wow!" breathed Nibbles. "The light changed its path!"

"Exactly!" Lark declared, her eyes sparkling brighter than the flashlight beam. "Light likes to travel straight, like a fast race car. But when it zooms from the air into water, it bumps into it and has to change direction. It bends! That bending light is what makes the pebble and your finger and the twig look all wobbly and broken, even when they're perfectly straight underneath!" She named the wonderful trick. "It’s called refraction!"

Nibbles splashed a paw in the water, sending tiny droplets flying. "Light bends? Wow! That's incredible!"

Lark nodded, a huge, triumphant grin spreading across her face. "It’s like when you look through a window at a distant tree, or see your reflection in a puddle! It’s all the bending light playing its tricks."

She carefully lifted the striped pebble out of the water. It was still a perfect, straight pebble, its stripes crisp and clear. "This is amazing! The water plays tricks with light, making everything look so different!" Nibbles nudged a bright blue feather, its edges delicate and soft, into the jar. It looked wonderfully wavy, like a tiny, dancing ribbon. "More bending!" he squeaked happily, his whiskers twitching.

"Today," Lark declared, holding up the now-straight pebble she’d taken out, her voice ringing with excitement, "is going to be AMAZING! There are so many more things to test and see how light bends them!" Ms. Rowan chuckled, her eyes twinkling like the stars Lark had just mentioned. "I suspect you two clever explorers will discover all sorts of wonders today." And with a skip and a happy bound, Lark and Nibbles were off, ready to investigate every ripple, every reflection, and every drop of water, eager to find out what other amazing secrets light held, just waiting to be discovered.
characters: Lark the water tester, Nibbles the otter, Ms. Rowan
